rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants Satan the opportunity to tempt people, while His sincere and true servants remain beyond Satan's lure.
rows.anchor: only sincere servants of God would not be led away by him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term ṣalṣāl means mud that has dried and begins to ring.
rows.anchor: mud that becomes dry and starts to ring.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ḥamaʾ masnūn denotes black, foul-smelling mud.
rows.anchor: refers to black and stinking mud.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All living beings originated in water and mud; land-dwelling creatures received a habitat and the capacities needed to live and grow there.
rows.anchor: All living beings originated from water and mud.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans also passed through water, mud, and dry-land stages, then were perfected in the strengths and potentials needed for their purpose.
rows.anchor: they have the distinction of being perfected with regard to their strengths and potentials

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the origin black, stinking mud reminds humans of their low origin and rebukes arrogance before God, who gave them profound abilities.
rows.anchor: it does not behoove a creature who was brought into existence from such a despicable ingredient to show arrogance before God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word samūm refers to flames of fire and scorching wind.
rows.anchor: refers to the flames of fire and the scorching wind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation materials are mentioned to explain the rivalry: Iblīs, a jinn, refused to prostrate because he considered his fiery origin superior, fueling lasting jealousy toward Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: the real purpose is to point to the basis of the rivalry between them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi says he discussed Adam and Iblīs in detail under Baqarah 22–38 and Aʿrāf 11–25, and limits repetition here to essential points.
rows.anchor: This incident of Adam (sws) and Ibl īs has been discussed in detail in this exegesis

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command for the angels to prostrate preceded Adam's creation; they were to prostrate after he was perfected and God's spirit was breathed into him.
rows.anchor: the directive given to the angels to prostrate before Adam (sws) was before he was created.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human distinction rests on perfected abilities and the divine spark: preserving these merits the angels' prostration, while wasting them makes a person worse than an animal.
rows.anchor: if he wastes them, he is only an animal; in fact, even worse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine spark is the source of spiritual advancement and connection with God when safeguarded; squandered, it leaves a person spiritually dark.
rows.anchor: It is this spark which is the fountainhead of all his spiritual advancements

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All the angels prostrated except Iblīs, who belonged to the jinn; he claimed that fire made him superior to the clay-made human.
rows.anchor: All creatures including those who are subsumed in their category prostrated except Iblīs, who was from among the jinn.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command was a test: the angels succeeded, while Iblīs refused arrogantly and was cursed for his rebellion.
rows.anchor: The angels succeeded in it but Ibl īs who was from among the jinn refused because of arrogance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs responds to the curse with still greater arrogance instead of shame, then challenges God.
rows.anchor: Instead of feeling ashamed and realizing his folly, Iblīs became even more arrogant.

rows.speaker: Iblīs
rows.claim: As Islahi explains Iblīs's accusation, Iblīs believed his refusal was right and implied that God's directive made obedience impossible, so God caused his deviation.
rows.anchor: Since Ibl īs regarded himself to be correct in not prostrating before Adam

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's temptations will engross people until they forget the status that earned the angels' prostration, the afterlife, and monotheism.
rows.anchor: they will be deeply engrossed in his temptations; they will not even remember their own status

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parallel in Aʿrāf 16–17 shows that Satan's basic aim is to turn Adam's descendants from God's straight path and monotheism toward polytheism.
rows.anchor: the basic target of Satan is to lead people away from monotheism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a small, fortunate portion of humanity will escape Satan's lures.
rows.anchor: only a few fortunate among mankind will be able to escape the lures of Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The monotheistic path threatened by Satan is straight, leads to God without hindrance, and is abandoned only by the wretched for a crooked path.
rows.anchor: from which Satan threatened to lead away people – leads to God and is not crooked.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the expression “this is a straight path to Me,” the particle ʿalā after dhā marks a style conveying that the path inevitably reaches its destination.
rows.anchor: this style is adopted when the purpose is to say that so straight is this path that it inevitably leads those who tread it to their destination.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd 11:56 illustrates that adhering to monotheism suffices to reach God; worship and trust in Him bring help through difficulty.
rows.anchor: adhereing to the straight path of monotheism is sufficient to reach God; no warped or twisted paths need to be traversed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi cites Naḥl 16:9 as a parallel: God's straight path reaches Him, while deviant paths depart from it.
rows.anchor: Similarly, in Sūrah al-Naḥl, it is stated:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word sulṭān means authority.
rows.anchor: The word 'ٌٰۡﺳﻠﻄﻦ means “authority.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes the fate awaiting those who follow Satan.
rows.anchor: The verse states the fate of those who will follow Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphasis on “all” answers Satan's boast that he would lead everyone astray: God likewise says He will fill Hell with them.
rows.anchor: that He too will fill Hell with everyone come what may.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell's breadth can accommodate the wrongdoers; its seven gates assign separate shares according to their crimes.
rows.anchor: Through each gate will they enter separately with regard to

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the passage coherently prevents the misconception that Hell cannot be vast enough to punish so many people.
rows.anchor: these verses mean no one should be under the misconception that how can such a vast expanse of Hell be available to punish so many people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi suggests seven principal categories of ruinous wrongdoing: polytheism, severing kinship, murder, fornication, perjury, oppressing the weak, and rebellion.
rows.anchor: they can be subsumed under seven principle categories referred to by the Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan tries to lead people to Hell by luring them into one or more of these wrongs.
rows.anchor: By luring people into one or all of these wrongdoings, Satan tries to lead people to Hell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing who follow God's directives live in harmony; disagreements fade when truth becomes clear, and God removes their lingering malice.
rows.anchor: They do not have any malice for one another and if there ever is any bad taste because of a difference of opinion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's varied favors keep its inhabitants from boredom despite their perpetual bliss.
rows.anchor: at every moment such will be the diversity and variety in God’s favours that the dwellers of Paradise will never feel any boredom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of remaining forever in Paradise assures its dwellers that their comfort will not end, removing the fear that would diminish temporary luxury.
rows.anchor: They will forever live in this life of luxury and comfort.
